advisories.detail: A ceiling of N admits N+1 total attempts (one initial plus N retries). Self-consistent and documented in RETRY_BINDING_LAW, but a reader-facing note should state that SourceAccessBudget.retries counts RETRIES, not attempts.

Only the outer MAXIMUM is a pre-operation gate; the outer EXACT is a post-operation postcondition. A hand-written spec that binds APPLICABLE with EXACT smaller than the admitted pass count (and an unbounded or larger maximum) performs source work and only then refuses. Unreachable from the seven-source warrant, which binds SRC27 expected 1 together with maximum 1, and NOT_APPLICABLE + EXACT 1 is still refused at bind.

A constraint naming an account the runtime does not have is not refused at bind; MAXIMUM and EXACT-0 on an unknown account are vacuously satisfied because a missing account reads as observed 0. No warrant-derived constraint depends on an unknown account.

BoundSourceExecution.session is a public accessor, so a holder can drive session.run() directly and bypass the outer gate. Recorded to bound the claim: this is a governed in-process entry point, not a sandbox. The commission already places cross-process uniqueness and host preflight outside this grain.
Unchanged from earlier waves: no real-source numeric reader-byte ceiling is source-free established, so the byte accounts remain UNBOUND_SOURCE_DEPENDENT and issuance-blocking rather than invented.
